cara: I opened a docs PR to add a Python SDK example for Optimize prefetch + microbatching and a short migration checklist for the new quant profile. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/894 :wave:

ravi: thanks — will review. Does the doc mention the short-sequence regression we saw in streaming benchmarks?

cara: yes, there's a dedicated "short-sequence streaming" callout under the batching section noting that prefix caching can increase end-to-end latency for many small requests. I added a suggested toggle: disable prefix cache for avg seq len < 8.

jamie: can you paste the Python snippet here? want to sanity-check the SDK surface.

cara: sure, minimal example below (redwood-python-sdk v1.2):

```python
# example: enable kv prefetch + microbatching
from redwood import RedwoodClient, OptimizeConfig, BatchConfig

client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
config = OptimizeConfig(
    prefetch=True,
    prefetch_window_ms=25,
    batch=BatchConfig(max_tokens=800, max_latency_ms=12),
    quant_profile="q4-adaptive-v2"
)
client.optimize.apply("service-abc", config)
```

cara: added the eval snippet to the migration checklist. It invokes our small-sweep evaluator and diffs a few metrics:

```bash
# quick eval: run on example prompts and compare to baseline
./tools/eval_small.sh --profile q4-adaptive-v2 --baseline q4-old --prompts tests/short_seq_prompts.json --out results/q4-adaptive-vs-q4-old.json
jq '.metrics | {ppl_diff: .ppl.delta, acc_diff: .accuracy.delta}' results/q4-adaptive-vs-q4-old.json
```

jamie: LGTM on the snippet. One API note: the Python class is OptimizeConfig not optimizeconfig in code block — looks correct here.
